messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: High 5xx spike for /v1/generate — 503s up 7x in the last 2m, p50 latency normal. Pager duty: @alex oncall.

alex: got it, I'm on it. Looking at dashboards now — opening the live HTTP error stream.

alex: quick note — customer-impact panel shows a handful of high-volume clients driving most of the spike. filtering by tenant cluster now.

maria: any autoscale events? I can toggle quota if needed.

alex: no scale events in the last 10m. worker GPU pools are healthy. This smells like request surge + backend overload; 429s creeping up too.

sre-lead: if it's surgey, can we apply temporary per-tenant rate caps and enable the lightweight fallback model?

alex: plan proposal: 1) apply soft throttle at edge (token-based limit for top offenders) 2) enable fallback compact model for non-enterprise routes 3) raise quota for critical enterprise customers only if they opt in. Thoughts?

ops-sig: +1 on soft throttle. Prefer to do incremental caps: 80% -> 60% if no improvement. Keep changes reversible.

alex: copying commands I'm about to run (will dry-run first):
```bash
# soft throttle key for tenant "alpha-corp"
redwoodctl quota update --tenant alpha-corp --qps 15 --reason "live emergency throttle"
# enable compact model route for non-enterprise
redwoodctl route set --path /v1/generate --model rwd-compact-v1 --selector "tier!=enterprise"
```

maria: I can patch the rate limiter config and watch metrics. I'll apply to top 3 tenants first.

alex: proceeding with dry-run on staging replica, results look promising — 503s down on replica. Going to roll to prod in 1m and monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy started: route patch rwd-compact-v1 -> /v1/generate (selector tier!=enterprise) by alex.

maria: applied soft throttle to alpha-corp and beta-io. Immediately seeing reduced request bursts on the request heatmap. 429s increased slightly for alpha-corp (as expected) but 503s are falling.

customer-support: hearing a few tickets from customers about slower responses — CS notified of temporary throttles. Can we add a banner?

alex: good call. I'll trigger a status page update and add banner to the dashboard. status: partial degraded for non-enterprise generation (temporary throttle).

sre-lead: keep an eye on error distribution: are 503s concentrated on a specific node pool or across many? If concentrated, we might need node-level remediation instead of throttling.

maria: distribution currently broad across pools, points to overloaded downstream service /kv-cache misses. Cache hit rate dropped ~30% during spike. We're adjusting cache size and warming prefixes.

alex: monitoring 429/503 timeseries now: p95 503 rate decreased 68% after throttles. Token cost drop as well.

ops-sig: decision log: temporary throttles + compact-fallback enabled at 1792506860. Reevaluate in 20m. If 503s remain low, gradually lift throttles. If not, escalate to infra for pool scaling.

maria: starting a 10m watch window. I'll also run spot-check prompts for quality regressions on the compact model and report if user-visible regressions > 5% on golden prompts.

alex: handoff note for next oncall (@sre-lead will take over after 30m): current state — throttles applied to top 3 tenants, compact fallback active, cache warming in progress, 503s trending down, 429s up slightly for throttled tenants. Next steps: monitor, prepare scaling if 503s resurge, coordinate with CS on customer comms.

sre-lead: I'll take over at 1792507000. Please leave runbook pointers.

alex: runbook snippet inserted into thread: "if 503s rise >2x baseline after 10m: 1) escalate to infra; 2) disable heavier features (batching) per service; 3) contact customers for manual quotas".

customer-support: we'll prioritize outreach for any enterprise customers who show >5% error rate.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: route patch complete at 1792506905.

maria: 20m check-in — 503s stable at baseline, compact model quality within acceptable bounds on our spot checks. Moving to passive monitoring.

sre-lead: taking active lead now. Good job. I'll coordinate a gradual rollback starting in 10m if metrics hold.

alex: thanks team. Leaving a short retrospective note: consider adding tenant burst protection in the edge proxy to avoid manual throttle dance next time.

ops-sig: noted for post-incident action item.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved -> monitoring. Duration: ~22m.
